1: Paul praises God, who chose us in Christ before the world was made, adopted us, redeemed us through his blood, and sealed us with the Holy Spirit. He prays that the readers may understand the hope they are called to. Christ is head over all things for the Church.
God's plan is to unite everything in Christ. Our lives are part of something planned from eternity.
2: We were dead in sin, but God, rich in mercy, made us alive with Christ. It is by grace, through faith, as a gift. Christ has broken down the wall between Jew and Gentile and made one new people, built on the apostles and prophets.
We are saved by grace, and created for good works. The Church is one household, with Christ as cornerstone.
3: Paul explains the secret now made known: Gentiles are fellow heirs with Israel. He kneels before the Father and prays that the readers may grasp the breadth, length, height and depth of Christ's love.
Christ's love is beyond knowledge, yet we are meant to know it. God can do far more than we ask or imagine.
4: Live worthy of your calling, with humility and patience. There is one Lord, one faith, one baptism. Christ gives apostles, prophets, pastors and teachers to build up the body. Put off the old self; speak the truth, and do not let the sun go down on your anger.
Unity is a gift to be guarded. Growing up in Christ means leaving old habits behind.
5: Walk in love; husbands and wives

Imitate God as beloved children. Avoid impurity and greed, and live as children of light. Husbands and wives are to give themselves to one another as Christ and the Church do; husbands must love their wives as Christ loved the Church and gave himself for her.
Marriage is a sign of Christ's love for his Church. The standard set for husbands is the cross.
6: Children should obey their parents, and fathers should not provoke their children. Paul then describes the Christian's armour: the belt of truth, the shield of faith, the helmet of salvation and the sword of the Spirit, the word of God.
Our real fight is not against other people but against spiritual evil. Prayer is how we stand firm.
